newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open off 0.3 to 0.4 cent.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open off 0.3 to 0.4 cent.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open lower Wednesday following slight softness in LME prices overnight.
COMEX September was called off 0.3 to 0.4 cent Tuesday's close of 104.85 cents a lb after trading from 104.35 to 105.00 cents on ACCESS.
LME warehouse copper stocks rose only 50 tonnes Wednesday to 254,350 tonnes, which was interpreted by London as mildly supportive.
COMEX copper stocks rose 577 short tons Monday to 33,869 short tons.
The LME cash-to-three month backwardation has narrowed to $16/$17 a tonne, the narrowest level since October 1996, which would appear to reflect ample availability in the physical market.

Falconbridge Ltd is expected to respond Wednesday to the latest local issue submitted by the Canadian Auto Workers at the Sudbury, Ontario, mine, which produces 50,000 tonnes of copper contained in matte.
The Ok Tedi mine in Papua New Guinea has halted shipments as a result of low water levels on the Fly River because of drought conditions.
